title: On-call triage cheat sheet and evidence mapping
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, on-call friendly triage cheat-sheet for security engineers responding to incidents that touch RBAC, audit logging, or SIEM evidence exports. It combines fast decision checklists, the minimal audit-log fields we need for evidence preservation, SIEM export sanity checks, and a short post-incident memo template so responders can hand off to investigations and leadership quickly.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to incidents where access control, suspicious admin activity, or the integrity/availability of audit logs/SIEM exports are in question.
- Assumes RBAC v2 is enabled in production (see RBAC-v2-design Confluence page).
- This is cross-functional: SRE for live traffic questions, Platform for Private deployments, Legal for potential disclosure.

Quick triage (first 10 minutes) — checklist
1) Confirm receipt and provenance
   - Slack #sec-oncall: confirm alert id, source (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk/Chronicle) and short summary.
   - Identify the triggered rule and sample event id(s). Copy/paste to incident channel.
2) Contain blast radius
   - If it's active malicious admin activity: immediately revoke privilege tokens/sessions for implicated principals via RBAC console -> forcibly expire sessions.
   - If model-serving or data plane impacted: open mitigation ticket in #platform-incident and consider traffic-shift to secondary region.
3) Preserve evidence
   - Snapshot the audit log segment (timestamps +/- 5m), take full event JSON. Export raw log to secure bucket (s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<incident-id>/raw-logs/).
   - Note time sync state (NTP offset) for host(s) involved.
4) Notify stakeholders
   - Ping incident manager, Legal, CTO on-call if scope > sensitive data or public risk. Use escalation matrix.

Severity quick classifier (use this to escalate)
- Sev 1: Active admin compromise or data exfiltration in progress, public-facing outage, legal/regulatory exposure.
- Sev 2: Suspicious privilege escalation attempts, failed audit pipeline, potential evidence gaps.
- Sev 3: Single-user anomalous behavior with low temper, or a noisy misconfiguration.

RBAC v2 checks (what to query immediately)
- Who: list the principal(s) involved (user/service-account/role).
- What: last 72h of role changes, policy updates, and group membership changes.
- Where: which environment/cluster/region was affected.
- Commands / console locations (internal quick links):
  - RBAC console: https://console.redwood.ai/rbac-v2 (use emergency revoke flow)
  - Audit view: https://console.redwood.ai/audit?principal=<id>&range=72h
- Quick actions:
  - Revoke role bindings: RBAC console -> principal -> revoke -> require reauth
  - Rotate credentials for implicated service accounts (generate key, update deployments, schedule rollback if needed)
  - Add temporary deny-list for IPs or principals at edge-proxy if suspicious traffic continues

Minimal audit-log schema (fields to capture for evidence)
- event_id (string) — unique id for the event
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601 string) — canonical event time
- observed_host (string) — host/instance id or region
- principal_id (string) — user/service-account/role id
- principal_type (enum) — {human, service, role}
- action (string) — e.g., policy.update, role.bind, token.create, model.invoke
- resource (string) — resource path (project/cluster/endpoint)
- outcome (enum) — {success, failure, denied}
- request_body_hash (string) — sha256 of request body for tamper evidence
- headers_summary (string) — sanitized headers (auth method, x-forwarded-for)
- trace_id (string) — correlation id for distributed tracing
- raw_payload_url (string) — S3/GS path for full raw event JSON

Why these fields: they allow reconstruction of who did what, where, and link to full payloads stored securely. For SIEM correlation we need event_id, timestamp, principal_id, action, resource, trace_id.

SIEM export sanity checklist (Splunk/Chronicle/Sumo)
- Confirm export completeness: compare event counts between audit store and SIEM for the incident window (t0-5m to t1+5m).
- Validate schema mapping: ensure event_id and timestamp_utc are in top-level fields and not buried.
- Ensure raw_payload_url is preserved in SIEM metadata (not redacted) or else copy it into the evidence bucket.
- Confirm retention policy applied (no auto-deletion before legal/forensics retention window) and note name of retention policy used.
- If export pipeline failed, trigger evidence automation fallback (see below).

Evidence automation triggers and play actions
- Triggers (examples):
  - RBAC policy change where actor is not in approved admins list -> auto-create evidence bundle + snapshot of policy repo commit + open JIRA-SEC-xxx.
  - Audit log export failure (parsing errors, schema mismatch) -> archive raw logs to fallback bucket and alert #sec-paging.
- Play actions (automated):
  - Create evidence bundle: collect audit segment, SIEM raw export, affected host snapshots, DB connection logs, and store to s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<incident-id>/bundle.tar.gz.
  - Tag bundle with metadata file (incident_id, created_by, trigger_rule, hashes) to support chain-of-custody.
  - Lock bundle (object-level retention) for 90 days; record lock action in audit log.

Containment quick recipes (fast ops commands)
- Disable a user's session/token: RBAC console -> principal -> sessions -> terminate. If console unavailable: call auth service endpoint /admin/sessions/terminate?principal=<id>.
- Revoke service account key: rotate key via GCP/AWS console and patch deployment. Use canary rollout.
- Block a compromised region: firewall rule add deny from <ip-range> to endpoints; route traffic to standby cluster.

Evidence handoff (template note to attach to bundle)
- incident_id: <id>
- summary: 1-2 sentence plain English summary of what happened
- implicated_principals: list
- time_window: t0..t1 (UTC)
- evidence_files: list of S3 paths
- immediate_actions_taken: bullets
- next_owner: investigator name and contact
- legal_hold_needed: yes/no

Post-incident memo template (fill quickly and iterate)
- Title: Incident <id> — brief descriptor
- Timeline: bulletized timeline (UTC) with source links to event ids
- Root cause hypothesis: short statement + supporting evidence ids
- Impact: systems, data, customers, business impact (quantify if possible)
- Mitigations: what was done immediately and what is planned (owner + ETA)
- Audit & monitoring changes: schema changes, new SIEM rules, retention edits
- Action items & owners: JIRA tickets assigned with due dates
- Disclosure recommendations: internal-only / customer notification / regulator notification (consult Legal)

Notes, gotchas, and heuristics (from folks who've triaged similar incidents)
- Don’t trust UI counts; always export raw events for the incident window and confirm via SHA256 hashes.
- When RBAC changes are detected, look for correlated CI commits or PR merges (possible legitimate change) before assuming compromise. Correlate commit id with audit event.request_body_hash.
- Keep a two-level evidence store: immediate hot-bucket for rapid analysis and a cold immutable bucket for long-term retention.

Open questions / TODOs (for doc owners)
- Define exact retention duration for evidence bundles for Private deployments (P0).
- Automate the session revoke API failover path (currently manual).
- Create a small runbook snippet for Legal/PR teams to use for customer communication drafts.

Appendix: quick links and useful commands
- RBAC console: https://console.redwood.ai/rbac-v2
- Audit logs raw store: s3://redwood-audit-store
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-sec-evidence
- Incident channel template: #sec-incident-<id>

If you use this doc while on call, drop a line in the doc history (append a short note) so we can iterate based on real incidents.

---
Revision note: created as compact on-call artifact; intended to be extended into a formal playbook after two production incidents.
